title: Cross-SDK error-signal matrix and idempotency harness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define a cross-language contract and a small runnable harness for classifying retryable errors, producing conservative default backoff profiles, and generating idempotency keys for request families (non-stream, chunked uploads, and resumable streams). Goal is consistent behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs with clear telemetry signals for operators and low-friction opt-out for application authors.
acceptance_criteria: Publish an error-signal taxonomy (transport vs transient vs user-error vs partial-result) with examples and canonical HTTP/gRPC mappings.
Provide three default backoff profiles (latency-sensitive, cost-sensitive, safe) with deterministic parameters and documented trade-offs.
Document idempotency key generation strategy per request shape (stateless prompt, file-chunk, interactive stream chunk) and provide helper functions in Py/TS/Go.
Deliver a small CLI harness that can replay recorded failures and validate SDK behavior against the taxonomy (recordings for HTTP status sequence and gRPC codes).
Add telemetry spans/tags spec for SDKs: retry_reason, retry_profile, idempotency_key, attempt_index, last_error_code.
Approve design with Lead SDK engineers and Security for KMS-related key handling flows.
implementation_notes: Design the taxonomy table with three axes: permanence (one-off vs persistent), visibility (server-specified Retry-After vs inferred), and consequence (duplicate-safe vs duplicate-harmful).
Backoff profiles should be simple: base_delay_ms, max_delay_ms, jitter_pct, max_attempts. Keep numbers human-readable and conservative for default clients.

Idempotency keys: use stable canonicalization of 'operation-signature' string + optional user-supplied id; for streamed chunks include stream_id + chunk_index + client-session-hash. Document when to let server dedupe instead.
The CLI harness records synthetic sequences (e.g., 503->timeout->200) and asserts SDK emitted telemetry and either retried or surfaced error according to profile.
Telemetry labels must be low-cardinality and opt-in by default for PII-sensitive fields; provide guidance for customers to sanitize idempotency_key before sending to telemetry backends.
Provide language-specific ergonomics: Python synchronous context manager for resumable streams, TS Promise/AsyncIterator helpers, Go context-aware functions returning resume tokens.
Consider exponent base 2 for latency-sensitive and 1.5 for cost-sensitive to limit token replays; safe profile uses linear backoff for a small number of retries then fails fast.
Ensure OpenTelemetry span attribute names are consistent across SDKs and map to Console dashboards.
Security review required for any helpers that persist idempotency keys to disk or integrate with KMS; design for ephemeral in-memory defaults.
